Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Ramesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A.
for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.51 of 2023, registered under Sections 41/411, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. at Police Station- Ashutosh @ Bikku Mishra vs State Of U.P. entities.text: Police Station- Ashutosh @ Bikku Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 Bargarh, District- Chitrakoot with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Although, the applicant is named in the FIR, but his name has come up in the statement of arrested co-accused persons Vipin Singh @ Nagesh and Ranchu Gautam, which is not admissible in evidence.
It is further stated that in all two cases have been foisted on the applicant and the another one is Case Crime No.156 of 2023, which has been instituted subsequent to the present FIR.
There is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.text: Ashutosh @ Bikku Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
